cells.tense: You are tending what's yours to tend, and the tending has your whole attention.
cells.ask: Let someone see what the tending has cost you, and let it be honored as a real sacrifice — that is what lets you set it down complete.
cells.core: You know what you're responsible for, and you're giving it what it actually needs — not what's easiest, not what looks best from outside, but the real thing. You see the pattern underneath, the way the parts depend on each other, and you work with that instead of against it. Two demands sit in your hands at once and neither one is winning. You hold both, and you hold them well. Nothing is being forced. The thing grows at the pace it grows, and your hands are steady on it.\n\nThat holding has a shape, and some of it is sacrifice. When someone names what the work has taken from you, the work is finished in a way that finishing alone never gives. Let the acknowledgment land, and let go. Release can be the reward, not the loss.
cells.sheetLine: You tend two things at once and you tend them well — let the cost be seen and set it down.
cells.verb: tending what you've been given to grow, by hand, for as long as it takes
cells.place: among the shapes of things — where you can see how a thing works without touching it

cells.tense: You are already standing in a future where this has grown wrong, and your hands are moving before it arrives.
cells.ask: Dream forward from what you've actually lived, not from what you're afraid of — let the vision come from experience and let experience settle first.
cells.core: Care is supposed to leave room for the thing being cared for to grow at its own pace. Instead the future has already arrived in your hands, and you're steering something that hasn't happened yet. You check on it, adjust it, guard it from outcomes nobody has seen, and the care has become the thing that wears it down.\n\nThe way back is not to care less. It's to let your imagination build on what's already been through you, not on the next thing you might lose. Vision that grows from what you've lived has a floor under it. Let that floor be there, and let today be enough.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing a future that hasn't arrived, and the managing is wearing the thing down.

cells.tense: You stopped tending, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Keep one hope alive out loud — say what you still want to grow, and let that wanting be what carries you back to the work.
cells.core: There's something in your care that went quiet — not lost, just not picked up again. The seeing is still there, still clear, still yours. What stopped is the reaching for it. You stand off to the side of the thing you know how to grow.\n\nThe way back is not to force yourself back into the work. It's hope — one thing you still want to grow, said plainly, kept warm and tended even before the doing starts. Care returns when you remember what it was for. Let one hope stay lit, and that light will walk you back to the garden.
cells.sheetLine: You still see what should grow — one hope kept alive is what carries you back to tending it.

cells.tense: You are already doing the work — your hands are in it right now — and you're calling it something other than yours.
cells.ask: Say plainly what this work has cost you and let someone acknowledge it — the sacrifice is real, and naming it finishes what silence has kept open.
cells.core: The tending is happening. You see what needs to be grown, you give it what it needs — the steady hand, the patient adjustment, the two demands held together. It's running right now, through you. What's missing is that you would say so. It goes into the account as circumstance, as what needed doing, as not-really-yours.\n\nSomething gets finished when its cost is named out loud and someone receives the naming. The work you've been doing in silence is asking for that. Not praise, not thanks — just the plain acknowledgment that this was yours and it asked something of you. Let that land, and let the thing be done.
cells.sheetLine: You're already doing it — name what it costs, let it be acknowledged, and let it be finished.
